content:
kai: hi team, i'm kai (starting today) trying to follow the runtime dev README. on ubuntu 22.04 with an RTX 4000. make fails during link: 
```/usr/bin/ld: /tmp/ccabc.o: in function `__device_stub__Z7kernelv': undefined reference to `__cudaRegisterFatBinary'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status```
anyone know the quickest fix?

neha: welcome kai! that specific symbol usually means the host linker isn't picking up the CUDA libs or nvcc wrappers. are you using system g++-11? Which CUDA toolkit did you install?

kai: toolkit /usr/local/cuda -> cuda-11.8, driver reports 525.x. i installed from deb. building on host, not container.

li: hey! two common causes we've seen: 1) nvcc compiling device code but the host linker (g++) is too new; we standardize on g++-9 for local builds. 2) missing `-lcudart` in the final link stage due to custom LDFLAGS.

neha: try this quick check: `nvcc --version` and `g++ --version`. then run: ```export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-11.8
export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
make clean && make -j4 CUDAVERSION=11.8```

kai: nvcc says 11.8, g++ is 11.3. switching to g++-9 now.

li: if you installed CUDA from the runfile sometimes the toolchain libs are in `/usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs` which confuses the linker. ensure `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` comes before stubs in LD_LIBRARY_PATH. also check `ldd ./libinference.so` to see which libcudart is being linked.

build-bot: note: CI builds in container image `redwood/runtime-dev:2026-01` with CUDA 12.1 and gcc-9. See last green build: https://ci.redwood-internal/runtime/5472

neha: if you want the fastest path, use our dev container: `docker run --gpus all -it -v $PWD:/workspace redwood/runtime-dev:2026-01 bash` then run `./scripts/local_build.sh`. It mirrors CI flags and avoids host toolchain drift.

kai: tried container, build moves further but now i hit compile errors in quant kernels: `error: no matching function for call to 'cuLaunchKernel'` — looks like headers mismatch?

li: that usually means the CUDA headers in the container don't match the toolkit version of the driver on your host. The container ships headers we compile against; when you bind-mount /usr/local/cuda from host into container it breaks things. avoid mounting system CUDA into the container.

ops-bot: added task: "complete runtime local build" to @kai in #runtime-onboarding checklist.

kai: removing the mount fixed the kernel headers error — build completed and unit tests are running. thanks for the help everyone. :pray:

neha: awesome — ping me or @li if tests fail. i also posted a tiny onboarding tip doc in #eng-runtime pinned messages.

kai: appreciated. will follow up if anything else pops up.
